nota: Words of this language that look borrowed from another language but do not exist there with that meaning, grouped by the language they imitate.

parole.testo: Pseudo-anglicism, derived from aerobics. While aerobic exists in English to refer to aerobics, it is an adjective and not a noun. First attested in 1984.
Pseudo-anglicism, a blend of aerobic + boxing. By surface analysis, aero- + boks. Compare Italian aerobox. First attested in the early 21st century.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from after-party.
Pseudo-anglicism, a blend of amputee + football.
Borrowed from French autocar, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English autocar. By surface analysis, auto- + car.
Borrowed from French auto-stop, and this a pseudo-anglicism, from auto- (relating to cars) + English stop.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from before party.
Borrowed from French body, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English bodysuit.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from boxing.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from boy.

Borrowed from English bungee. The sense "bungee jumping" is a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English bungee jumping.

parole.testo: From English church + Polish -ing, influenced by clubbing. Pseudo-anglicism.

parole.testo: Pseudo-anglicism, derived from happy ending.

parole.testo: Pseudo-anglicism, derived from leasing.

parole.significato: industrialist based in or around Łódź (especially one of German or Jewish descent)
parole.testo: From German lodzer + Mensch. Pseudo-Germanism. Coined by Polish writer and journalist Wincenty Kosiakiewicz in 1895 and later popularised by Władysław Reymont.

parole.significato: shame, cringe (cause or reason of shame; that which brings reproach and ignominy)
parole.testo: From żenować + -ada. Alternatively, a pseudo-Gallicism derived from gêner + -ade.
Borrowed from English hentai, and this a pseudo-Japonism derived from Japanese 変態(へんたい) (hentai); see that entry for more.

parole.significato: obsession (idea that engenders a compulsive or irrational preoccupation, or the preoccupation thereby engendered)
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, from fiksacja (cacoethes) and dyrdać (to go fast).
